US-China Agree to $30 Billion Tariff Cuts
On Friday, the White House said the U.S. and China reached consensus on more favorable tariff treatment for "$30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction," reported Reuters.
The arrangement covers U.S. exports including agricultural products, wood products and cosmetics, while Chinese goods receiving favorable treatment include small appliances, toys and decorations.
The two countries also operationalized the U.S.-China Board of Trade.
Xi Urged Human Control Over AI
On Thursday, Xi Jinping said the

params.linkText: U.S. and China had a shared responsibility

children: to ensure AI remained "under human control" and benefited people.
Trump said AI would be a key topic in discussions between the two countries as they prepared to establish a formal dialogue on AI risks and communication protocols.
Trump continued to favor Department of Justice oversight over broad AI regulation, saying, "Our guardrail is the DOJ."
He argued that stricter rules could slow the growth of a technology he believed could become bigger than the Industrial Revolution.
Trump said the U.S. would refer to applicable emerging AI technologies as "Super Intelligence" rather than artificial intelligence.
